note: How fast players move, react, catch and throw (docs/03 section 10, docs/09 section 7). Ratings are 1..99; each pair is the value at rating 1 and at rating 99. 'basis': S = MLB Statcast averages, A = assumption tuned with ./dev sim --physical.

top_speed_ms.basis: S: 27 ft/s = 8.23 m/s average, 7.0 to 9.3 range

acceleration_tau_s.basis: A: v(t) = v_max (1 - e^(-t/tau)); with the start delays below an average runner gets from home to first in about 4.3 s and steals second in about 3.5 s

batter_leaves_box_s.basis: A: contact to the first running step (finishing the swing and dropping the bat)

batter_to_first_m.basis: plate to first base less where the batter stands

base_path_factor.basis: A: rounding a base swings the runner wide, so a path over two or more bases is this much longer than the straight lines (3 to 6 %)

rounding_base_s.basis: A: extra time to round a base instead of stopping at it

slide_gain_m.basis: A: a slide reaches the bag this much sooner than a runner standing on it, at the cost of the speed lost sliding

secondary_lead_m.basis: A: extra ground gained as the pitch is delivered

runner_read_s.basis: A: a runner's start after contact on a ground ball

two_out_jump_s.basis: A: with two out the runner is already moving in his secondary lead and runs on contact: this much ahead of a standing start

steal_jump_s.basis: A: from the pitcher's first move to the runner's first step

delivery_s.basis: A: pitcher's first move to the catcher's mitt, docs/09 section 7 (by hold rating)

reaction_s.basis: A: an infielder's first step on a ground ball, set in his ready position: about 0.2 s for an MLB average fielder (rating 60; the KBO average is 50, docs/09 section 7)

outfield_reaction_s.basis: A: reading a ball in the air before committing (outfielders always, infielders on liners and pop-ups): about 0.47 s at rating 60

backward_speed.basis: A: running back on a fly ball

reach_m.basis: A: from the middle of his body to the glove; a running catch reaches a little less far than standing tall

transfer_s.basis: A: glove to throwing hand to release

catcher_transfer_s.basis: S: catcher exchange about 0.7 s, so an average arm gives a 2.0 s pop time

outfield_extra_transfer_s.basis: A: setting the feet and the crow hop; an outfielder fielding a single gets rid of it in about 1.1 s

throw_kmh.basis: S: Statcast arm strength 126 to 146 km/h averages by position

throw_speed_kept.basis: A: average speed over a throw's flight against release speed

relay_beyond_m.basis: A: a longer throw goes through a cut-off man

pivot_s.basis: A: turning a double play at second, about 0.5 s

tag_s.basis: A: putting the glove down on a sliding runner

runner_judgment_sd_s.basis: A: how far off a runner's guess of a close play can be

catch_chance.air_basis: Proposal 2 (approved 2026-11-21): Statcast Catch Probability shape (distance and opportunity time, harder going back and at the wall; star bands 0-25%, 30-50%, 55-75%, 80-90%, 95%). S-curve of the time to spare; half catches at air_half_s, tuned with ./dev sim --physical to keep the league's hits on fly balls

errors.basis: A, tuned with the error target (0.673 per team per game)

runner_aggression_s.basis: A: margin a runner (and the coach) wants before trying for the next base; with two out he goes even on a slightly losing read

long_throw_scatter_s.basis: A: a long throw is off line or short-hopped now and then: spread of its arrival per 40 m beyond 40 m

catcher.basis: A: what the catcher can catch cleanly

hit_by_pitch.basis: the batter's body as a cylinder, A for the dodge
